summary: Reads the text of a UI screen widget via UIScreenTextAccessor, locates the last path-delimiter (word_5C692C) occurrence in a copy of the text, skips a2 delimiter-separated components by repeatedly locating the preceding delimiter, and copies the suffix from the final delimiter position into the this+0xE1 (225) output buffer; returns a pointer to that buffer. Returns 0 if the widget has no text or no delimiter is found. Legacy ABI label: UI_Text_Format_Helper.

operations.description: Initialize the stack buffer: v12[0] = byte_5EA438[0], then memset the remainder (0x4C bytes plus the v13/v14 tail) to 0.
v3 = UIScreenTextAccessor(this) fetches the widget's text; guard: return 0 when NULL.
Set the output-buffer pointer v4 = this + 225 (offset 0xE1) and clear its first byte: *(this + 225) = 0.
Copy the widget text string from v3 into the stack buffer v12 (null-terminated copy).
v7 = sub_5897CA(v12, &word_5C692C) finds the last path-delimiter occurrence in the copied text.
When a2 > 0, repeat a2 times sub_5897CA(0, &word_5C692C) to walk back across a2 delimiter-separated path components.
Return 0 when v7 is NULL after the delimiter search.
Copy the suffix string from v7 (the final delimiter position) into the this+0xE1 output buffer (null-terminated copy).
Return v4, the pointer to the output buffer at this + 225 (offset 0xE1).

clean_pseudocode: for (int i = 0; i < skip; ++i) d = sub_5897CA(0, &word_5C692C);
unresolved: sub_5897CA is only identified as a delimiter locator (strrchr-style, per existing analysis); its behavior when its first argument is 0 (used in the skip loop) is inferred, not proven here.
Ownership of the 'this' object and the exact meaning of the this+0xE1 buffer (a path/name suffix for a UI list) depends on the caller UIListManagementHandler (0x0048A3C0).
The legacy ABI label UI_Text_Format_Helper (abi:lead) is retained as weak (LEGACY) naming evidence only.
